title: One finite etale-origin evaluation of intrinsic refinement is invertible
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell and a field k of positive prime characteristic different from ell [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let f:X -> Y be a k-morphism between separated finite-type k-schemes and w:c -> d a proper compactification refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the actual strict semilinear coefficient-system category and its positive-level derived evaluations [def-pur-semilinear-compact-support-coefficient-transport, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], the quotient-coordinate equivalence [def-pur-integral-support-comparison-data, def-pur-adic-exceptional-system-realization], and the actual systemRefinement:F_d -> F_c [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Fix any Brown site comparison V for X [def-pur-brown-system-site], an ordinary derived coefficient system M and one index n. Suppose the n-th evaluation of coordinates(M) is isomorphic to the inverse site image of an etale derived object H bounded below. Then evaluation at n of systemRefinement(w).app M is an isomorphism. No lower bound or etale origin is imposed at any other level, and M need not be normalized.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; parent node proof Step 1, finite-level part before joint conservativity.

proof.text: Use the actual semilinear proper/open mate evaluation equation to identify the chosen n-th evaluation of the refinement with the constant finite-ring proper/open mate, including the identity-edge map and the proper compositor. Exact quotient coordinates preserve sections, and the canonical site realization factors identify the supplied etale witness with an etale origin for this finite-ring mate.

The n-th quotient of the integer ring is finite. Transport the lower bound of H through the exact coefficient realization. The constant finite-coefficient proper/open invertibility theorem applies at this level. Its comparison identifies the evaluated mate as an isomorphism. The evaluated proper compositor and identity-edge maps are already isomorphisms; their composite, the evaluated systemRefinement, is therefore invertible. Only invertibility is transported, and no equality detection by evaluation occurs.

theorem systemRefinementEvaluation_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [NormedField E]
    [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ l)]
    (X Y : CondensedERealization.Base k) (f : X.scheme ⟶ Y.scheme)
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] {c d : Compactification f} (w : c.Refinement d)
    (P : StrictEtaleEvaluation X.scheme (integralExceptionalIntegers l E)
      (integralExceptionalUniformizer l E))
    (V : BrownTowerComparison.Site X.scheme (integralExceptionalIntegers l E)
      (integralExceptionalUniformizer l E) P)
    (M : coefficientSequenceDerived.{u, u} l E X.scheme) (n : ℕ)
    (_hM : ∃ H : DerivedCategory (strictEtaleLevel X.scheme
      (integralExceptionalIntegers l E) (integralExceptionalUniformizer l E) n),
      (∃ a : ℤ, H.IsGE a) ∧
        Nonempty ((V.comparison.evaluation.level n).inverse.obj H ≅
          (V.proEvaluation.evaluation n).obj ((coordinates l E X.scheme).functor.obj M))) :
    IsIso ((coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y.scheme n).map
      ((systemRefinement l E k X Y f w).app M))
